current_state.question_reconstruction_note: All 50 QuestionIntents were inspected against their authoritative vertical semantics and compiler publication projection. Full Concept/Relation/Indicator ID arrays remain authoritative in the source files and are intentionally not mirrored into a competing research authority.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶5, PDF p.10; Figure 3, PDF p.49
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Aggregate recovery is uneven: labor-intensive construction/manufacturing lag stronger agriculture, mining, energy and financial activity.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶6, PDF pp.10–11; Figure 4, PDF p.50
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Headline inflation can diverge from underlying measures as food, regulated prices, inertia, demand and FX pass-through contribute differently.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶7 fn.4, PDF p.11
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Backward-looking indexation can temporarily raise real indexed spending during disinflation.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶9, PDF p.12; Figure 6, PDF p.52
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Real peso appreciation can coexist with BCRA FX purchases and reserve rebuilding.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶10, PDF pp.12–13; Figure 6, PDF p.52
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Strong energy/agriculture exports can be offset in the current account by imports, services and income outflows.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶10–11, PDF p.13; Box 7, PDF p.44; Figure 6, PDF p.52
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Gross FX purchases, gross reserves, NIR and liquid buffers differ because financing liabilities, debt service and other balance-sheet items matter.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶11, PDF p.13; Staff Appraisal, PDF p.35
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Recent reserve/market improvement can coexist with weak reserve coverage, large FX obligations and incomplete durable market access.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶12, PDF pp.13–14; Figure 7, PDF p.53
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Rapid real private-credit growth can coexist with tighter allocation and rising consumer NPLs.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶12 and fn.11, PDF p.14
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Resident FX purchases may remain in domestic bank deposits rather than mechanically becoming external outflows.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Recent Developments ¶13, PDF p.14; Structural Policies ¶34, PDF pp.28–29
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Approved or announced strategic investments are not the same as realized fixed investment or productive capacity.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Outlook and Risks / baseline, PDF pp.15–18
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Projected growth, FDI and export expansion can frame questions but should not become Atlas measurement truth.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Box 3, PDF p.40
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Higher global energy prices can raise inflation and subsidy pressure while improving terms of trade and hydrocarbon exports.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Monetary/FX ¶26–28, PDF pp.23–25
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Reserve purchases, remonetization and disinflation interact because money-demand recovery affects how reserve accumulation is absorbed.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Authorities' Views ¶29, PDF p.26
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Authorities caution against reading a one-way causal effect from reserves to sovereign spreads because both share other drivers.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Monetary/FX ¶27, PDF p.24; Financial Sector ¶30, PDF p.26; Figure 7, PDF p.53
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Lower market rates do not automatically imply easy credit when NPLs and risk constraints still tighten lending conditions.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Financing Policy ¶24–25, PDF pp.22–23; Exceptional Access, PDF pp.33–34
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Repos, guarantees and domestic-law FX issuance can bridge financing needs without proving durable international market access.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Box 8, PDF p.45; Figure 2, PDF p.48
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: A high credit growth rate is compatible with a financial system that remains shallow as a share of GDP.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Structural Policies ¶33–34, PDF pp.27–28; Figure 2, PDF p.48
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Short-run output recovery does not establish productivity convergence or durable capacity deepening.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Structural Policies ¶34, PDF p.28
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Primary-sector expansion can precede broad employment gains when labor-intensive sectors and spillovers lag.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Data Quality and Adequacy ¶43, PDF p.32; Monetary/FX ¶28, PDF p.25
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: CPI weights and national-account base/granularity can matter for interpretation even when official data remain authoritative.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Box 1, PDF p.38; Figure 3, PDF p.49
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Poverty changes combine labor income, basic-basket-relative inflation, pensions and transfers rather than headline CPI alone.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Box 7, PDF p.44
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Peso/liability-side BCRA balance-sheet repair can coexist with a deeply negative net FX position.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Box 8, PDF p.45; Figure 7, PDF p.53
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Financial deepening should be read beside capital/liquidity buffers, NPLs and funding structure.

imf_bridge_findings.locator: Figure 3, PDF p.49
imf_bridge_findings.paraphrase: Sector activity, GDP contributions, employment composition, real wages and poverty form one connected recovery story.

cue_candidates.text: Gross reserves are not the same as net or immediately usable external buffers.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Do not infer NIR or adequacy from a gross-reserve stock chart.
cue_candidates.why_cue: Adds the missing interpretation without duplicating the reserve ontology.

cue_candidates.text: BCRA FX purchases are one reserve flow; debt service, financing and other balance-sheet changes also move NIR.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Does not identify the size of each flow without dedicated measurement.
cue_candidates.why_cue: Clarifies stock/flow arithmetic more cheaply than a new semantic object.

cue_candidates.text: Fast credit growth can coexist with a shallow financial system when lending starts from an unusually low base.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Growth rates and credit-to-GDP levels answer different questions.

cue_candidates.text: Lower market rates do not by themselves mean easy credit when asset quality and bank risk constraints are tightening.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Descriptive context only; not a causal estimate of bank supply.
cue_candidates.why_cue: Joins rate and credit evidence without a new transmission object.

cue_candidates.text: Aggregate recovery can strengthen while labor-intensive sectors remain weak, so sector breadth matters alongside the headline index.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Sector activity alone does not measure employment intensity.
cue_candidates.why_cue: Explains why q.re01 is the opening Real question.

cue_candidates.text: Higher fixed investment is more informative when its construction and machinery components are separated.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Composition does not by itself establish productivity effects.
cue_candidates.why_cue: Adds capacity interpretation without a new indicator family.

cue_candidates.text: Rising imports can signal recovering domestic demand while simultaneously weakening external-balance arithmetic.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Real volumes and nominal current-account values are not directly equivalent.
cue_candidates.why_cue: Makes a cross-region tension legible without causal language.

cue_candidates.text: Reserves and sovereign spreads share common drivers; co-movement should not be read as one-way causality.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Authorities' view is a caution, not causal proof.
cue_candidates.why_cue: The question already exists; only the interpretation guard is missing.

cue_candidates.text: Real appreciation can coexist with FX purchases and reserve accumulation; interpretation depends on the wider balance of payments.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Does not label the exchange rate over- or undervalued.

cue_candidates.text: Resident dollar buying need not equal capital flight when FX deposits remain inside the domestic banking system.
cue_candidates.interpretation_limit: Requires deposit/flow evidence to know the split in any episode.
cue_candidates.why_cue: Clarifies a common public vocabulary ambiguity.

priority_actions.why: Unlocks the strongest future Real opening and several subordinate questions.
Brings an already-public reserve question into alignment with its own semantics.
Turns aggregate investment into capacity-composition intelligence.
The plot layer already crosses this boundary; the graph should expose it.
Connects public Nominal rate evidence to the future Real transmission question.
Makes Real demand and External arithmetic visibly connected without inventing causality.
Balances the credit-deepening story with risk evidence.
Preserves a thin public hierarchy around breadth, drivers and investment.
Prevents stock/flow and causal reserve misreadings.
Persistent statistical caveats change epistemic presentation and need methodological judgment.

real_economy_review.assessment: The vertical has the right semantic ingredients for a thin opening, but activation should be evidence-gated rather than question-count-gated.

recommended_future_public_spine.reason: Best synthesis of broad versus concentrated recovery.
Explains which demand/trade components drive aggregate growth.
Best bridge from cyclical recovery to durable capacity; q.re06 is the composition drilldown.

supporting_not_leading.reason: Useful consumption component of the growth-driver story.
High-value drilldown once investment-composition measurement is bound.
Historical/reference framing rather than a leading public promise.
